observation.visible_scene: A large square mosaic portrait (a stylized face) built from thousands of upright, multicolored domino-like blocks lies flat on a light wooden floor. A separate wavy line of standing dominoes runs along the bottom edge and up the left edge, meeting the mosaic at its bottom-left corner. The camera viewpoint and the floor/mosaic layout stay fixed throughout.
visible_changes: From t=0 to t=0.2 the mosaic is fully upright and the scene is static.
Around t=0.2 a small cluster of blocks at the bottom-left corner of the mosaic begins to topple, lying flat and exposing a smooth, lower-textured surface.

This fallen zone grows steadily as a diagonal collapse front: the boundary between upright (still showing the pixelated image) and fallen (flat, muted) blocks sweeps from the bottom-left corner toward the upper-right and right side across the remaining frames.
By t=1.0–1.5 the flat fallen region covers most of the lower-left quadrant and extends diagonally upward; the standing portion is confined to the upper-right area and a central band.

Near the end (t=2.0–2.67) the front reaches the right edge, and the dark blocks at the bottom-right corner also begin to lie flat, while the long horizontal trigger line along the very bottom and the left-edge line remain standing and unchanged.

The collapse is a progressive toppling (deformation of the standing field into a flat field), not a translation or removal of the mosaic; the overall square outline and face image persist in the still-upright region.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the remaining upright blocks on the right/top eventually fall, and the final state of the mosaic.
The exact mechanism that initiated the corner topple relative to the bottom/left trigger line (the line itself stays standing within the excerpt).
uncertain_details: Camera motion appears absent (background floor planks and mosaic position do not shift), but only a fixed view is confirmable.
The first few frames (t=0–0.13) are effectively identical, so the precise instant of onset is bracketed between t=0.13 and t=0.2.
